newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS - Analysts see Olivetti link limited.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Analysts see Olivetti link limited.

text.p: Telecoms analysts were sceptical on Monday that French privatisation target France Telecom was set to take a stake in struggling Italian technology group Olivetti.
Despite newspaper reports of talks between the two groups, analysts said they believed current talks were aimed a cementing a fixed-line telecoms link.

The talks between the French state telecommunications operator and Olivetti are likely to see France Telecom enter Olivetti's Infostrada venture, confirming a growing alliance on fixed-line telecoms in the last 10 months.
"I would be very, very surprised if France Telecom with its privatisation looming in the spring would make a risky investment in Olivetti," said one London telecoms analyst.
Olivetti's investment in fixed-line telecoms has been through its Infostrada joint venture with Bell Atlantic of the United States, which holds 33 percent, and the rest by Olivetti.
"Clearly, France Telecom is interested in the Italian market and its best way to advance this is by formalising its close links with Infostrada," said a Milan-based industry analyst.

Both Olivetti and France Telecom declined to comment directly on a report in the International Herald Tribune that France Telecom was looking at a new strategic alliance and eventually buy an equity stake in Olivetti.

The two groups have been talking together since last November when Olivetti's Infostrada announced a joint venture with France Telecom to set up Italy's second major fixed-line telecoms network to herald the first true competition for the state-controlled Telecom Italia.

The two groups moved closer in August when Infostrada and France Telecom reached a draft agreement to buy a 70 percent stake in the Italian state railway's domestic phone network in a deal worth 600 billion lire ($400 million).

"After the railways deal, it would seem logical for France Telecom to enter the Infostrada venture," said the London-based analyst. The Herald Tribune said France Telecom was looking to buy 49 percent of Infostrada.

France Telecom has not hidden its interest in the lucrative Italian market, and has said it aims to be the second biggest fixed-line operator in Italy. Analysts said an Italian partner would be France Telecom's best way forward, and at the moment that points to Infostrada.
But they pointed out it was unlikely to want to take a stake in Olivetti ahead of its planned privatisation next year, with question marks hanging over Olivetti.

Olivetti has made a loss for the last five years, and its ex-director general in charge of finance and auditing Renzo Francesconi resigned this month after expressing doubts over the validity of the group's first-half 1996 financial accounts.

France Telecom wants to be an early entrant into Italy before the deregulation of the Italian telecom market in 1998. In addition, the Infostrada/France Telecom deal to create Italy's second-fixed line operator will bring in the backing of big international groups Deutsche Telekom and U.S. Sprint.
Analysts added that France Telecom would probably like also to be involved in the Omnitel consortium, Italy's second mobile phone operation where Olivetti has a 41.7 percent stake.

But under Omnitel's licence, 60 percent of its shareholders cannot be changed before February 2000. This effectivily locks in its three largest shareholders Olivetti, and U.S. groups AirTouch and Bell Atlantic, so limiting the entry of any new groups into the consortium, analysts said. ($1= 1,523 lire)
